speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: asked	the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (a) what is the current number of students studying in international schools in Singapore; (b) how many of them are foreigners; and (c) whether the Government is promoting the private education industry as one of the key engines of economic growth, and if so, whether there are plans to increase the number of international schools and the student numbers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: They cater primarily to the children of international executives based in Singapore.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Besides international schools, other commercial players also offer private education to Singaporeans and foreigners.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: The private education landscape is diverse, with varying quality in courses and providers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The original Parliamentary Question was about international schools, as an engine of economic growth, with respect to how they support the international companies and their families.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, if Members would like to delve deeper into the private education sector or the development of the faculty of these institutions, and so on, can I invite the Member to file a separate Parliamentary Question directed at the Ministry of Education (MOE), so that we can respond comprehensively and accordingly?
